_meta.notes: Comprehensive index for the Democratic Republic of the Congo covering Bantu migration, Kongo, Luba, and Lunda kingdoms, King Leopold's Congo Free State (rubber terror), Belgian Congo, Lumumba assassination, Mobutu/Zaire, Congo Wars (Africa's World War), Kabila era, and conflict minerals.

910.name: Early Peoples and Bantu Migration
910.description: Hunter-gatherer Pygmy peoples (Mbuti, Twa) inhabit the Ituri rainforest; Bantu-speaking farmers migrate into the Congo Basin bringing agriculture and ironworking.

sub_clusters.name: Mbuti, Twa, and Forest Peoples
sub_clusters.description: Indigenous hunter-gatherer communities in the equatorial forest; symbiotic relationships with later Bantu farming arrivals.

sub_clusters.name: Bantu Expansion into the Congo Basin
sub_clusters.description: Bantu-speaking farmers spread across the Congo Basin; introduce iron smelting, pottery, and banana cultivation; population growth transforms the landscape.

920.name: Kongo Kingdom
920.description: The Kongo Kingdom, centered on Mbanza-Kongo, becomes one of Africa's most powerful states; early contact with Portugal; Christianity adopted; kingdom fragmentsover time.

sub_clusters.name: Foundation and Expansion of Kongo
sub_clusters.description: Lukeni lua Nimi founds the Kongo Kingdom; capital at Mbanza-Kongo; control of trade in copper, iron, raffia, and nzimbu shell currency.

sub_clusters.name: Portuguese Contact and Afonso I
sub_clusters.description: Diogo Cão reaches Kongo 1482; King Afonso I converts to Christianity; diplomatic relations with Portugal and the Vatican; slave trade begins.

sub_clusters.name: Battle of Mbwila and Kongo Decline
sub_clusters.description: Kongo defeated by Portuguese at Battle of Mbwila (Ambuila) 1665; king killed; kingdom fragments into warring factions; civil wars until 18th century.

920.name: Luba and Lunda Empires
920.description: The Luba and Lunda empires dominate the savanna of southeastern Congo; sophisticated political systems, copper/salt trade, and far-reaching influence.

sub_clusters.name: Luba Empire
sub_clusters.description: Luba kingdom in the Upemba Depression; sacred kingship (mulopwe); elaborate political philosophy; copper-cross currency; ironworking centres.

sub_clusters.name: Lunda Empire and Mwata Yamvo
sub_clusters.description: Lunda Empire expands under the Mwata Yamvo title; extensive tributary system; trade in slaves, ivory, and wax reaching both Atlantic and Indian Ocean coasts.

sub_clusters.name: Msiri's Yeke Kingdom (Katanga)
sub_clusters.description: Nyamwezi trader Msiri establishes Yeke Kingdom in copper-rich Katanga; controls long-distance trade; killed by Belgian expedition 1891.

930.name: Slave Trade and European Exploration
930.description: Atlantic and East African slave trades devastate the population; Arab-Swahili traders penetrate from the east; Stanley's exploration opens the Congo to European imperialism.

sub_clusters.name: Atlantic Slave Trade from Congo
sub_clusters.description: Millions enslaved from the Congo region; Loango, Cabinda, and Kongo ports; internal wars fuelled by demand for captives; demographic catastrophe.

sub_clusters.name: Arab-Swahili Slave and Ivory Trade
sub_clusters.description: Tippu Tip and other traders establish slaving networks from Zanzibar deep into eastern Congo; Manyema devastated; Nyangwe massacre 1871.

sub_clusters.name: Stanley's Exploration of the Congo
sub_clusters.description: Henry Morton Stanley traverses the Congo River 1874–77; later signs treaties for Leopold II; maps the Congo for European exploitation.

940.name: King Leopold's Congo Free State (1885–1908)
940.description: King Leopold II's personal colony; rubber terror regime kills millions; mutilations and forced labour; international outcry leads to Belgian takeover.

sub_clusters.name: Berlin Conference and Congo Free State
sub_clusters.description: Berlin Conference (1884–85) recognises Leopold's International Association as sovereign of the Congo; Force Publique established; rubber exploitation begins.

sub_clusters.name: Rubber Terror and Atrocities
sub_clusters.description: Forced rubber quotas enforced by mutilation (hand-cutting), hostage-taking, and murder; population estimated to have halved; Casement Report (1904) and E.D. Morel's campaign expose horrors.

sub_clusters.name: Belgian Annexation (Belgian Congo)
sub_clusters.description: Belgium annexes Congo Free State 1908; paternalistic colonial rule; mining economy (Union Minière du Haut-Katanga); limited African education; no political rights until late 1950s.

950.name: Independence, Lumumba, and Congo Crisis
950.description: Rapid decolonisation; Patrice Lumumba becomes first PM; Congo Crisis erupts with Katanga secession, Lumumba assassination, and UN intervention.

sub_clusters.name: Independence and the Congo Crisis
sub_clusters.description: Congo independent 30 June 1960; Force Publique mutiny; Katanga secession under Tshombe; Lumumba assassinated January 1961 with Belgian and CIA complicity; UN intervention.

sub_clusters.name: Katanga Secession and Resolution
sub_clusters.description: Moïse Tshombe declares Katanga independent backed by Belgian mining interests and mercenaries; UN operations end secession by January 1963.

950.name: Mobutu and Zaïre (1965–1997)
950.description: Mobutu Sese Seko seizes power; renames country Zaïre; Authenticité campaign; Cold War ally; massive corruption; economic collapse; ousted by AFDL.

sub_clusters.name: Mobutu's Coup and Consolidation
sub_clusters.description: Lieutenant-General Mobutu seizes power November 1965; single-party MPR state; nationalises Union Minière (Gécamines); Zaïrianisation of economy.

sub_clusters.name: Authenticité and Cold War Patronage
sub_clusters.description: Country renamed Zaïre; Authenticité campaign; Shaba invasions repelled with Western help; Mobutu as Cold War anti-communist ally; kleptocracy hollows out the state.

sub_clusters.name: Mobutu's Decline and Fall
sub_clusters.description: Cold War ends; Western support withdrawn; sovereign national conference; Rwandan genocide spillover; Laurent-Désiré Kabila's AFDL marches on Kinshasa; Mobutu flees May 1997.

960.name: Congo Wars: Africa's World War
960.description: Two Congo Wars (1996–97, 1998–2003) draw in nine African nations; estimated 5.4 million excess deaths; deadliest conflict since WWII.

sub_clusters.name: First Congo War (1996–1997)
sub_clusters.description: Rwanda and Uganda back AFDL; Rwandan Hutu refugee camps dismantled; Kabila topples Mobutu; DRC declared.

sub_clusters.name: Second Congo War (1998–2003)
sub_clusters.description: Kabila turns against Rwandan/Ugandan allies; nine African nations involved; RCD and MLC rebel groups; Lusaka Ceasefire; Laurent Kabila assassinated January 2001; Joseph Kabila succeeds.

960.name: Post-War DRC: Kabila Era and Beyond
960.description: Transitional government; Joseph Kabila's presidency; delayed elections; Felix Tshisekedi elected 2019; ongoing eastern insurgency; conflict minerals.

sub_clusters.name: Joseph Kabila Presidency
sub_clusters.description: Joseph Kabila oversees transition; elections 2006 and 2011; refuses to leave after term expires; eventually transfers power to Tshisekedi 2019.

sub_clusters.name: Eastern DRC: Endless Insurgency
sub_clusters.description: Over 100 armed groups in Kivu; CNDP, M23, ADF-NALU, Mai-Mai; Rwanda-backed M23 captures Goma 2012 and resurges 2022–2023; MONUSCO peacekeeping.

sub_clusters.name: Conflict Minerals and Resource Curse
sub_clusters.description: Coltan, cobalt, tin, and gold fund armed groups; DRC holds world's largest cobalt reserves critical for batteries; Dodd-Frank Section 1502; artisanal mining abuses.

sub_clusters.name: Tshisekedi Presidency
sub_clusters.description: Félix Tshisekedi wins disputed election January 2019; breaks coalition with Kabila's FCC; re-elected 2023; M23 crisis and Rwanda tensions escalate.

unassigned_events.note: Events not yet assigned to a thematic cluster
